name: Glassjaw
label: Warner Bros.
lede: Two campers from Long Island made a debut on Roadrunner, quit the label and told fans to stay away from it. The third album took fifteen years, and Amazon leaked it first.

eras.title: Two kids from summer camp
eras.text: Daryl Palumbo and Justin Beck met at camp and grew up on New York hardcore: Youth of Today, Bad Brains, Sick of It All. Six years of lineup changes on Long Island ended when producer Ross Robinson heard a demo.

years.h: Daryl Palumbo and Justin Beck meet at camp and start a band
years.p: Beck liked Swiftkick as a name, but Glassjaw won out, after passing through xGlassjawx and The Glassjaw.

years.h: Glassjaw plays Oceanside, New York, for the first time
years.p: The South Shore Long Island town is near Palumbo's hometown of Bellmore.

years.h: Palumbo is diagnosed with Crohn's disease
years.p: It becomes the subject of the first album's title track and the reason for years of canceled dates.

years.h: Kiss Kiss Bang Bang arrives on 2 Cents a Pop
years.p: Palumbo, Beck, Todd Weinstock, Kris Baldwin and Ariel Telford play on the EP. Star Above My Bed is still in the setlist decades later.

years.h: Beck goes from drums to bass to guitar
years.p: He started on drums, moved to bass when Ariel Telford left in 1998, and takes up guitar when Kris Baldwin leaves and Manuel Carrero comes in on bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Glassjaw · Wikipedia: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Silence
years.h: Ross Robinson hears the demo and wants in
years.p: Robinson gets Glassjaw's demo and talks Roadrunner Records into signing the band. Beck remembers him jumping up at practice, shouting that he'd do it.
years.xp:
That year the band also recorded with producer Don Fury. Then it went to Indigo Ranch in Malibu with Robinson to make its debut.

By then the lineup had settled around Manuel Carrero on bass, Todd Weinstock on guitar and Sammy Siegler on drums.

eras.title: A war with Roadrunner
eras.text: The debut gave Glassjaw a name, and the label that put it out became the enemy. By the end of 2001 the band was telling fans to download it.

q: It's stupid, you don't speak face-to-face to a woman like that.
years.src: Wikipedia: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Silence
years.h: A debut recorded in two months at Indigo Ranch
years.p: Robinson produces Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Silence in Malibu, with [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] on drums. NME hears Jeff Buckley doused in napalm.
years.xp:
NME's full line was "Jeff Buckley doused in napalm, crawling through a room full of broken glass." The title track is about Palumbo's Crohn's diagnosis, but most of the songs deal with relationship pain, and the record has been criticized for misogyny. After a 2017 Pitchfork piece on sexism in emo, Palumbo said as much.

Robinson said the plan was to take down the Adidas rock of nu-metal bands like Limp Bizkit. The album reached No. 82 in the UK and, per Wikipedia, sold more than 47,000 copies in the U.S. Metal Hammer put it at No. 1 on its 2022 list of essential post-hardcore albums.
play: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Silence

years.h: Six weeks in Europe behind Deftones and Soulfly
years.p: Larry Gorman of [[Orange 9mm|66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51]] takes over the drums for the road.

years.big: "Seriously, don't ever support anything from Roadrunner - they suck!"
years.h: Roadrunner and Glassjaw split in public
years.p: Justin Beck's parting advice to fans. The band says the label barely promoted the debut and wouldn't let Palumbo rest when Crohn's flared on tour, and urges fans to download the album.
years.xp:
Palumbo called Roadrunner "a joke" and a "miserable fuckin' corporation." Ross Robinson, who produced the album, said the aim from the start was to destroy Adidas rock.

Glassjaw was already working on its second album with Robinson. Four years later, Palumbo and Beck both turned up on Roadrunner United: The All Star Sessions.

eras.title: Warner Bros., and a hospital in Paris
eras.text: On Warner Bros., Glassjaw made its second album and then couldn't tour it: Palumbo's Crohn's disease put him in hospitals in Paris and Glasgow. By late 2004 the band's website read RIP.

years.h: Warner Bros. puts out Worship and Tribute
years.p: Robinson produces again, with [[Shannon Larkin|736a6ab6-1b97-4b5f-a36e-dc7e295e8715]] of [[Godsmack|ac2d1c91-3667-46aa-9fe7-170ca7fce9e2]] on drums. It debuts at No. 82 on the Billboard 200, Glassjaw's only entry there.
years.xp:
Weinstock said the songs were written around the September 11 attacks, and it colored the tone. Pitchfork later called it a "genre-defining work"; NME called it the greatest underground breakthrough album since Deftones.

The song Convectuoso was cut with Roadrunner for a single. When Glassjaw moved to Warner, Roadrunner kept the rights and wouldn't release it, and it only appeared on the 2022 vinyl reissue, after Roadrunner joined Warner Music Group. Singles: Cosmopolitan Bloodloss (December 2002) and Ape Dos Mil (April 2003).

years.h: A summer on Warped and Ozzfest, with Dave Allen on bass
years.p: Glassjaw works the big summer tours, plus Snocore, with Allen now in the bass slot.

years.h: A Crohn's relapse puts Palumbo in a Paris hospital
years.p: Intestinal surgery wipes out the German and UK dates. He relapses again in December.
years.xp: Palumbo was rushed to the hospital in Paris on October 1. On December 5 he was hospitalized again, in London, and more European dates fell through.

years.h: Glasgow hospital, then the London Astoria falls through
years.p: Palumbo is hospitalized in Glasgow. Glassjaw cancels more shows, including the Kerrang! Weekender and the London Astoria.

years.h: Palumbo puts out Decadence with Head Automatica
years.p: [[Head Automatica|5e94030f-c3c7-4777-a5af-5ecfbfc37bba]] is Palumbo's pop side band, with Gorman on drums. Beck spends the time building his merchandise company.

years.h: The website reads RIP Glassjaw as three members go
years.p: Guitarist Todd Weinstock, bassist Dave Allen and drummer Larry Gorman are fired. The band denies it has split and points to Palumbo's Crohn's disease.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes the RIP header was possibly a joke. The band came back in 2005 as a four-piece.

eras.title: 100% maybe
eras.text: Glassjaw came back as a four-piece, played rarely, and spent years recording an album nobody heard. When Warner Bros. restructured, the band left with its tapes.

years.h: Carrero and Lang make Glassjaw a four-piece
years.p: Manuel Carrero returns on bass and Durijah Lang takes the drums; nobody replaces Weinstock. The band plays three shows, including a charity benefit in Farmingdale and a spot with [[The Used|8262d8e4-9137-4bb3-a787-3caabbbc13e9]] at Hammerstein Ballroom.

years.h: El Mark collects B-sides from Worship and Tribute
years.p: Glassjaw's first release in three years is leftovers from the Warner Bros. album.

years.h: Deftones tour, then the Fucking Tour 2006
years.p: Glassjaw supports Deftones and headlines a run of its own, then plays New Year's Eve with [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]] at Connecticut's Stillborn Fest.

years.h: Glassjaw headlines Brixton, its first UK show in four years
years.p: The Carling Academy date is July 7. The band later calls its Southern California run the 100% Maybe tour.

years.h: Beck has thirteen songs done and no vocals yet
years.p: Beck, producing with engineer Jonathan Florencio, has drums, bass and guitar finished, including Jesus Glue and a reworked Star Above My Bed.

years.h: Warner Bros. and Glassjaw part ways
years.p: The split follows a corporate restructuring and a dispute over Palumbo's shelved Head Automatica album Swan Damage. The band keeps its recordings.

years.h: Carrero and Lang leave Saves the Day to go all in
years.p: Both quit [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]] to make Glassjaw their only band.

eras.title: The biggest DIY band in the world
eras.text: Free of labels, Glassjaw sold new songs through Justin Beck's merch company, on dates that matched their titles, and Rock Sound called it the biggest DIY band in the world. Then the rhythm section left.

years.h: A 7-inch you can't play without the plastic logo
years.p: On 8/8 at Hevy Fest, Glassjaw sells All Good Junkies Go to Heaven on spray-painted vinyl that needs a die-cut logo to play. It sells out in hours.
years.xp: The logos came free, hidden in merch packages or sent out on random postcards. The dates kept matching the titles: Jesus Glue on 9/9, Natural Born Farmer on 10/10 and You Think You're (John Fucking Lennon) on 12/12, which sold out instantly. Buying merch got you the songs as free downloads.

years.h: Our Color Green (The Singles) goes digital
years.p: The 2010 vinyl singles are collected into one EP and released to iTunes, Amazon and eMusic.

years.h: Coloring Book is free at the door
years.p: After the first show of the tour, Glassjaw gives the EP to everyone at the venue. Gold streamed first, at 11:11 a.m. on January 11.

years.h: Sonisphere gets canceled, so Irving Plaza gets Worship and Tribute
years.p: Glassjaw books the New York club and plays its 2002 album start to finish.

years.h: Carrero and Lang walk after a decade
years.p: The rhythm section later joins the reunited [[Burn|502429d5-da95-4a78-bfc9-7c8cf93504e6]]. Lang said he had no axe to grind and just ran out of reasons not to call it a day.

years.h: Travis Sykes and Chad Hasty debut at Amityville Music Hall
years.p: Both come from Glass Cloud, and the show is a surprise date on Long Island.

years.h: Opening for Coheed and Cambria with songs nobody has heard
years.p: Glassjaw supports [[Coheed and Cambria|ae1b47d5-5128-431c-9d30-e08fd90e0767]] in the UK and U.S. and plays small headline shows full of new material. In December, [[Billy Rymer|b6587c65-10ca-4c64-bc37-dd02f7ce7a72]] of The Dillinger Escape Plan says he tracked a whole album of drums.

eras.title: Fifteen years late
eras.text: The third album leaked from Amazon fifteen years after the second. After that the band spent its anniversaries playing the old records.

years.h: A third album, fifteen years late, leaks from Amazon
years.p: An Amazon listing puts Material Control out on November 15, two weeks before Century Media's December 1 release. Buyers from Beck's MerchDirect got a ten-song flexi-disc.
years.xp: Rymer plays drums on the twelve tracks. The album reached No. 7 on the U.S. Independent chart and No. 12 on the Rock chart. Shira came out as a single on November 24, with a video in April 2018, and a video for Golgotha followed on June 28.

years.h: Glassjaw and Quicksand split a summer tour
years.p: Walter Schreifels' [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] co-headlines the U.S. run behind Material Control.

years.h: Twenty years of Worship and Tribute, played in full
years.p: Glassjaw plays its first two albums in full for their anniversaries. The Worship and Tribute vinyl reissue finally includes Convectuoso.

years.cap: Daryl Palumbo and Justin Beck, Los Angeles
years.h: Glassjaw is booked on Warped Tour again
years.p: The 2026 lineup comes 24 years after the Worship and Tribute summer on the same tour.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Silence
